title: Branching & Checkout
html:
Creating parallel lines of development to build features in isolation.

Branch

A Branch in Git is a lightweight, moveable pointer to a specific commit. By default, projects start with a default branch (typically main). Creating a new branch creates a separate pathway of history so you can build features or fix bugs without affecting the stable production code.

Branching Flow Chart

Commit 1
→
Commit 2 (main)
→
Commit 3 (main)
Commit 2 (main)
↳ checkout new branch →
Feature Commit A
→
Feature Commit B

Branching Commands

CommandPurposeDescription
git branchList BranchesLists all local branches in the repository.
git checkout [branch]Navigate BranchSwitches the working directory to the target branch.
git checkout -b [new-branch]Create & NavigateCreates a new branch and switches to it in one step.
git branch -d [branch]Delete BranchDeletes a branch (requires that changes are merged).
Interview tip

On modern versions of Git, the checkout command can be replaced with git switch (e.g. git switch -c new-branch to create and switch), separating branch navigation from file restoration.
